prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1047; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a collision at an intersection in which the insured vehicle was turning left and was struck on the driver's side by another vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photos submitted by the insured, which show damage to the left front quarter panel and door that lines up with the impact described in the first report. Body shop estimate requested.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the sequence of events as the insured described it. Independent witness statement obtained and it matches the same account.

Entry 4: Police report obtained. It records the collision location, the direction of travel of both vehicles, and the damage noted at the scene, all consistent with the claim.

Entry 5: Claimant reports a wrist fracture from the impact. Medical records requested through counsel. The injury type and the force of the crash appear consistent with one another based on the vehicle damage review.

Entry 6: Claimant's account has been the same in each contact so far, including the first call, the recorded statement, and the follow-up with counsel present. Exact seating position in the vehicle at impact is still not fully clear and is being followed up.

Entry 7: Vehicle history checked. No prior damage to this vehicle is on record, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy effective period. Prior medical history for the same body area has been requested and none is known so far.

Entry 8: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this type of fracture. Records show the claimant has been seen by several providers, and the billing is being reviewed against the treatment notes.

Entry 9: Confirmed that the driver involved is a household member of the policyholder and qualifies as a covered driver under the policy.

Entry 10: File is progressing toward a settlement evaluation once the remaining medical records and the seating position question are resolved. Next review scheduled with counsel.
